**Where we are ahead:** a drop-in `std.mem.Allocator`, so every std container and arena that takes an allocator wipes its growth copies without code changes; `SecureAllocator` adds `sodium_malloc`'s guard pages, canary and `mlock`. **Where we are behind:** no allocation tracking or quarantine, no in-place growth variant (→ *What is deliberately not done*).

## What this module is, and what it is not

`WipingAllocator` is a small `std.mem.Allocator` adapter: `alloc` forwards,
`free` calls `std.crypto.secureZero` over the whole block before `rawFree`,
`resize` returns `false`, `remap` returns `null`. It was five identical private
copies (xmlenc, xmldsig, wireguard `wipe.zig`, bbs `burn.zig`, minisign
`burn.zig`) and is the one place they now share.

Reference behaviour: OpenSSL `OPENSSL_clear_free` and libsodium `sodium_free`
cleanse a block before releasing it; neither offers an in-place shrink that
skips the cleanse, which is what refusing `resize`/`remap` reproduces.

**Not here, by design:**

- **`mls`'s `Wiper`** (`modules/mls/src/group.zig`) is a different allocator, not a
  copy: it forwards *grow-in-place* `resize` to the child (growing hands nothing
  back) and refuses only shrinks and remaps, because it sits under an
  `ArenaAllocator` whose last chunk is extended in place. It stays private.
- **Stack burns** (`burn.stack`, `burn.run`): per module, `burn.zig` is copied on
  purpose (CONVENTIONS §2.1 D3: each module's stack probe measures its own frames).
- Test spies (`ScanAllocator`, `Spy`, `DirtyAllocator`) in other modules observe or
  corrupt memory; they do not wipe.

## Constant-time contract

No secret-dependent branch or address: the wipe is a volatile byte-store loop
over `memory.len`, a public length. The module makes no timing claim beyond that.

## Limits and refusals

- `resize` is always refused, `remap` always returns null (a caller's `realloc`
  therefore always copies). Pinned by "resize and remap are refused…" and
  "realloc moves through alloc + copy + free…".
- The adapter must outlive every block and must not move (the vtable points at it).
- Cost: one volatile store per byte on `free` (`std.crypto.secureZero`); a module
  that wants vector-width wipes can link `fastmem` for the whole binary.

## Secure allocator (`SecureAllocator`)

`SecureAllocator.init(lock)` (Linux; `getrandom` draws its canary) is a separate allocator for a handful of keys, after
libsodium's `sodium_malloc` and OpenSSL's `OPENSSL_secure_malloc`. Per block: one anonymous mapping of
`guard page | data pages | guard page` (the guards `PROT_NONE`), the data pages `mlock`ed (`Lock.best_effort` goes on
unlocked when `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` refuses, `.required` fails the allocation, `.off` does not try) and `MADV_DONTDUMP`ed, a
16-byte per-allocator random canary directly in front of the block, and the block placed as far toward the upper guard
as its alignment allows (a block whose length is a multiple of its alignment ends exactly at the guard, so any overrun
faults). `free` checks the canary (`@panic` when overwritten, as libsodium aborts; `canaryIntact` for a caller that
wants to ask), zeroes every data page with `secureZero` and unmaps the whole mapping (which also unlocks it).
`resize`/`remap` are refused. A block of alignment above the page size, of length 0, or whose pages would pass 1 TiB
is `null`. Cost: two system calls and at least three pages of address space per block. Tests (`src/root.zig`): guard
pages on both sides and the data pages readable (`process_vm_readv` reports `EFAULT` for an unreadable page
without a signal), alignment up to the page, the canary per allocator and its detection, `realloc`, `Lock.required`
under `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` of 0 (skipped when the limit cannot be set), and an unmapped block after `free`.

## Anchoring

Expected values: the spy child's view of the block (all zero), the data after a
`realloc`, the bytes of a backing buffer after an `ArrayList` grew and was freed.
Our own reading of the contract.

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

## What is deliberately not done

- **No allocation tracking and no quarantine** (libsodium's `sodium_malloc` does
  these): this wipes on free and nothing else. **Never.**
- **An in-place growth variant** (what `mls`'s private `Wiper` does under its arena:
  grow-in-place `resize` forwarded, shrink and `remap` refused): neither OpenSSL nor libsodium offers
  a growing wipe, and `mls` is the only consumer, so a second allocator type here would serve one caller
  that already has it. Reopen when a second consumer needs it.
- **A `realloc` for `SecureAllocator`** (neither libsodium's `sodium_malloc` nor OpenSSL's `OPENSSL_secure_malloc`
  has one): `resize`/`remap` are refused, a growing buffer is alloc + copy + `free`.

## Verification

- **Run:** `scripts/modtest wipealloc`.
- **Tests** (`src/root.zig`): a spying child allocator sees an all-zero block on `free`; `resize` and `remap` are refused
  for growth, shrink and same size; `realloc` growth and shrink wipe the old block and keep the data; the wipe covers
  the whole block at every alignment and a zero-length free is harmless; an `ArrayList` that grows behind the adapter
  leaves no secret in the child's freed blocks; `init` and the struct literal are the same adapter and an
  allocation failure passes through.
- **Fuzz / constant time:** n/a (see the card's `Hardening` line).
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and
  the delta runs after it.
- **Mutation 2026-11-25** (whole module: `SecureAllocator` was ~53 % of it): 32 mutants, 29 killed, 2 equivalent (the
  `dataLen` overflow checks are subsumed by the 1 TiB cap), 1 unobservable (the wipe before `munmap`: nothing can read
  the pages in between without a seam), 0 open. New tests: rounding and the cap, a zero-length request, `mlock` (VmLck)
  and `MADV_DONTDUMP` (smaps `dd`), `free` unmaps the whole mapping (mincore), a canary overwrite aborts (forked child).
